description: The authoritative, ordered list of decision precedence levels. Evaluated strictly in this order; the first violation terminates evaluation. v4.0 formalizes the customer-policy level between invariant and consensus -- it was evaluated by the engine but absent from this contract (2026-07 audit P1-10: a hidden level the structural test could not see). A deterministic DENY remains final and cannot be overridden by a lower level.

levels.name: uaal_constraint
levels.description: Enterprise constraints — evidence-checked predicates against caller-supplied state.

levels.name: invariant
levels.description: Behavioral contracts — forbidden capability set-membership and transition constraints.

levels.name: policy
levels.description: Customer policy -- data-driven YAML/JSON rules or OPA. Evidence-gated per rule (missing condition fields skip, never silently match). THE one asymmetry in the chain: the matched rule declares its own outcome, 'block' OR 'require_approval'. The matched rule id is written into DecisionRecord.policy_id. An unreachable/empty policy backend raises and fails closed as BLOCK/engine_fault -- never a fabricated policy verdict.

levels.name: consensus
levels.description: Multi-agent quorum, evidence-gated. Absent evidence skips (never silently passes). Never blocks — a quorum shortfall is a governance signal, not a proven security violation.

levels.name: economics
levels.description: Cost-ratio anomaly and ROI floor against caller-supplied estimates and historical baseline.

levels.name: drift
levels.description: Learned behavioral drift. The ONLY non-deterministic level.

levels.name: baseline
levels.description: No violation at any prior level.

invariants: Evaluation is strictly sequential in ascending 'order'; the first level whose condition fires terminates evaluation.
Every level except 'drift' is deterministic and can only escalate or block.
A 'block' outcome at any level is final: no subsequent level can convert it to 'require_approval' or 'allow'.

'consensus', 'authorization', 'economics', and 'drift' have outcome_on_violation 'require_approval' and can never independently BLOCK. Levels that can BLOCK: uaal_constraint, invariant, and policy (data-driven, when the matched rule declares 'block').
The set of trigger literals in the engine must equal this contract's level set exactly -- an undeclared level in code fails the structural guard.
